title: Telemetry stewardship swimlanes and compact panel guide
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a compact, operational-friendly approach to telemetry stewardship for inference features that are rolling out in H1. Goal: reduce operator cognitive load during incidents while keeping panels useful for engineers doing root-cause analysis.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: oncall SREs and feature owners for serving/runtime teams.
- Secondary: product engineers for Dedicated/Private features that affect latency/cost.
- Scope: token-serving latency, KV cache metrics, batching efficiency, fallback flows, and model-routing traces. Not covering embedding infra (separate catalog).

High-level proposal (one-line):
Assign lightweight metric stewards (1 per major signal area), define 3 compact operator panels per service, and adopt a 3-tier trace sampling policy tied to customer tier + anomaly detection.

Stewardship swimlanes (who does what):
- Metric steward (owner): maintains metric definition, alert thresholds, and small query snippets. (Owner: service or platform team.)
- Dashboard steward: responsible for panel ergonomics, query cost, and runbook links. (Usually the same person as metric steward early on.)
- Trace steward: maintains sampling knobs, redaction rules, and span enrichment. (Infra/observability team.)
- Cost steward: tags metrics/dashboards with cost tags and monitors query budgets monthly.

Suggested compact operator panels (per runtime service):
1) Operator at-a-glance (Top priority for SRE):
   - 99th wall-clock latency (user-facing path) by quantile, delta vs baseline, tenant hotlist (top 5 cost/latency tenants).
   - Active batch size distribution (p50/p90), batch formation rate, batching dropouts metric (requests falling back to single-shot).
   - KV cache hit ratio (prefix/kv cache separate), cache effectiveness (tokens saved per 1k requests).
   - Error rate (5xx, model-fallback count) with immediate runbook link.
2) RCA starter panel (for engineers):
   - Token-level latency breakdown: request enqueue, scheduling wait, first-token, steady-state per-token.
   - Model queue depth, GPU utilization per node pool, memory pressure warnings.
   - Trace-sample quick links: session id search, representative spans for last 5 slow requests.
3) Cost & rollout panel (product + infra):
   - P50 token-cost-per-request, quantization profile usage, inference shape mix (seq lengths).
   - Routing policy impacts: percent traffic routed to cheaper model variants, fallbacks to larger models.
   - Canary vs baseline divergence chart (latency + quality drift placeholders).

Metric definitions (compact, copyable):
- user_request_99_latency_ms: "p99 end-to-end server latency in ms measured at ingress gateway normalized to request start"
- kv_prefix_hit_rate: "ratio of requests served from prefix/KV cache within 200ms vs total requests"
- batching_efficiency_pct: "1 - (average tokens / ideal-batch-size) expressed as % where ideal-batch-size is workload-specific target"
- model_fallback_count: "count of requests that used fallback model variant due to capacity/latency SLO triggers"
- tokens_saved_by_cache_per_1k: "estimated tokens avoided because of KV/prefix cache per 1000 requests"

Tracing sampling policy (practical recipe):
- Baseline sampling: 1% random sampling across all requests for retention of general telemetry.
- Tiered amplification: multiply baseline by 10x for premium customers and 2x for dedicated capacity tenants.
- Anomaly-driven capture: automatic 100% capture for sessions where p99 latency > threshold (service-specific) OR error rate spike > baseline + 3 sigma for 5min window.
- Ad-hoc capture: oncall can flip a short-lived capture flag for a deployment ID (TTL 1h) to capture 100% for targeted investigation.
Implementation note: enforce PII redaction at collection point (span attributes) and strip full prompt text unless explicitly opt-in and stored in secured bucket.

Tracing enrichment suggestions (span tags):
- tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, batch_id, batch_size, kv_hit=true/false, seq_len_estimate, cpu_ms, gpu_ms

Runbook sketches (quick links go to longer runbook):
- High p99 latency: check operator at-a-glance batch sizes -> if batch sizes collapsed to 1, suspect scheduling contention; check GPU queue depth and node autoscaler events.
- High model_fallback_count: check route policy changes, capacity scaling logs, and model-loading errors in model-serv logs.

Dashboard cost controls and query quotas:
- Each dashboard must include estimated query cost in comments header (simple 3-line estimate).
- Tag dashboards with cost-center: e.g., cost_center:serving-runtime or cost_center:dedicated-sales.
- Monthly budget: Enable UI to disable non-operator dashboards when remaining query budget < 10%. (Product work.)

Migration playbook for new signal onboarding (short):
1) Feature owner proposes metric and draft query in a ticket (JIRA/PR).
2) Observability review (1-week review, quick meeting slot) -> steward assignment.
3) Pilot: expose metric on a staging compact panel for 2 weeks.
4) Promote to prod operator panels and set alerts.
5) Postmortem after two incidents or 3 months, whichever comes first.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we collapse cache metrics (prefix + kv) into one rollup for low-traffic tenants? (tradeoff: signal fidelity vs panel simplicity)
- Exact anomaly thresholds for auto-capture need tuning per service. Propose a small experiment: run 100% capture for 1% of traffic for 2 weeks and compare signal quality.
- How to elegantly show per-tenant cost without leaking across teams in multi-tenant dashboards? Need RBAC work.

Next steps (practical):
- Assign metric stewards for serving-runtime, optimize, and private-deployments by EOW. (Aisha -> follow up.)
- Prototype a compact operator panel for the inference gateway and measure query cost for 1 week. (Liam + Evelyn)
- Draft JIRA template for telemetry proposals (short fields: metric, owner, dashboard, cost estimate, retention TTL). (Carlos)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally compact. If it grows, break into two docs: (1) stewardship process + templates, (2) panel designs + example queries.
